about: A 64-bit integer is carried on as a <param> of a <send> as the text of its digits, and read back from it: `wide.in` brings a uint64 `big` and an int64 `small`, the machine sends them to itself as `wide.relayed` with `small` made one less, and keeps the remainders of the two by 1000, which a double that rounded a value past 2^53 would get wrong. A 64-bit field is read from a text of its digits, or from a JSON number up to 2^53 - 1; a number past that, digits with a leading zero and a minus sign on an unsigned field are refused on every engine, so a payload gives one field wherever it is read. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: 2^53 + 1 and -(2^53 + 1) arrive as digits and cross as digits: the low digits are the ones sent
a number a double holds exactly is read as a number
the widest of each signedness: 2^64 - 1, and the signed minimum once it is made one less
the signed minimum does not fit once it is made one less: the pair is left out, the message goes and its receiver refuses it
a number past 2^53 - 1 is not exact everywhere, so it is refused where it is read
digits with a leading zero are no canonical spelling of a number
an unsigned field has no minus sign
a good delivery after the refused ones is carried on as any other
